query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy whose low hardness and poor friction and wear properties limit its use under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties. State the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, applicable operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) applied to TC4 for around 18 hours can refine its grain structure and promote β-phase transformation to a harder α′-phase, thereby improving both hardness and wear resistance without compromising its tensile strength, plasticity, or toughness.
generation.material_initial_state: Unmodified α + β dual-phase TC4 alloy, which inherently has low hardness and suboptimal wear properties under high-contact-stress conditions.
generation.intervention: Expose the TC4 alloy to deep cryogenic treatment at −196 °C for an extended period (approximately 18 hours).
generation.conditions: Testing and operation under ambient environments simulating extreme service with high friction and contact stresses; laboratory wear and hardness tests (e.g., pin-on-disk and Vickers hardness) conducted under controlled conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced grain refinement and increased fraction of α′-phase relative to the β-phase following DCT.
generation.mechanism: The DCT process induces a phase transformation that converts β-phase to the harder α′-phase and refines the grain structure. This microstructural evolution results in increased resistance to plastic deformation (improving hardness) and, indirectly, enhances wear resistance while preserving or even enhancing the alloy’s toughness and ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated TC4, the DCT-treated alloy will exhibit approximately a 9–10% increase in hardness and reduced wear rates, while maintaining similar tensile strength and improved toughness and plasticity.
generation.baseline: The untreated TC4 alloy with a typical hardness of around 331.2 HV0.5 and conventional wear performance under high-contact stress conditions.
generation.boundary: The benefits are expected within the specific treatment regime (−196 °C for ~18 hours) and may not extrapolate to durations significantly shorter or longer, which could lead to insufficient transformation or potential embrittlement.
generation.uncertainty: While increased hardness and improved toughness following DCT are evidenced, the direct correlation with enhanced wear resistance in TC4 remains less directly documented and requires experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of identical TC4 alloy samples. Apply 18 hours of deep cryogenic treatment on the experimental group while keeping a control group untreated. Subject both sets to standardized wear tests (such as pin-on-disk) and Vickers hardness tests, as well as microstructural analysis via XRD and SEM.
measurements: Vickers hardness (HV0.5) before and after treatment
Wear rate and friction coefficient in pin-on-disk tests
Phase composition and grain size assessments using XRD and SEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the DCT-treated samples do not show a statistically significant increase in hardness (at least 9–10% improvement) and a corresponding reduction in wear rate, or if detrimental changes occur in tensile strength or toughness compared to the untreated baseline.

## Abstract
AbstractDeep cryogenic treatment (−196 °C, DCT) is an emerging application that can make significant changes to many materials. In this study, DCT was applied to Ti6Al4V (TC4) titanium alloy, and we delved into an examination of the impact on its microstructural morphologies and mechanical properties. It was observed that DCT has a significant effect on the grain refinement of the TC4 titanium alloy base material. Obvious grain refinement behavior can be observed with 6 h of DCT, and the phenomenon of grain refinement becomes more pronounced with extension of the DCT time. In addition, DCT promotes the transformation of the β phase into the α′ phase in the TC4 titanium alloy base material. XRD analysis further confirmed that DCT leads to the transformation of the β phase into the α′ phase. The element vanadium was detected by scanning electron microscopy, and it was found that the β phase inside the base material had transformed into the α′ phase. It was observed that DCT has a positive influence on the hardness of the TC4 titanium alloy base material.
